summary: "The Iran War is About to Make (More) Millionaires" (Business With Brian, 2026-04-24) argues the market is fixated on oil while six supply lanes feeding the tech stack flow through the same Strait of Hormuz choke point: oil, helium (Qatar produces 33% of global supply, South Korea sources 64% of its helium from Qatar, fabs carry only 2-4 weeks of inventory, no substitute), sulfur (the Gulf produces 44%; ultra-pure sulfuric acid cleans every wafer and sulfur extracts copper), aluminum, noble gases for lithography lasers, and petrochemicals for chip packaging — all up 10-18% since the conflict began. He layers on Taiwan's vulnerability (48% of electricity from LNG with Qatar the largest supplier at 34%, last nuclear reactor shut in 2025) and red-hot memory demand: DRAM/SSD prices +130% YoY, OpenAI's Stargate locking up 900K DRAM wafers/month (40% of global output), HBM consuming 20% of wafer capacity for 8% of bits, with SK Hynix and Micron's entire 2026 output pre-sold.
